profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting within IEA PVPS Task 13 between the workstream leading the multi-site yield-assessment benchmark compilation and the workstream preparing the downstream cash-flow/LCOE linkage. Context: the consortium has already collected independent yield assessments for several PV sites spanning desert, temperate, tropical, and snowy climates, and now needs to align the interface between the technical benchmark package and the economic modeling package before a shared internal deadline. Agenda: confirm which benchmark result set will be handed over, what counts as the 'baseline' and the 'uncertainty reduction scenario' package, how site files and assumptions will be versioned, and what the economic team should expect in the deliverables. Expected outcome: both participants leave believing they have agreed on the handoff format, timing, ownership of the master benchmark sheet, and the level of processing to apply before the LCOE team starts ingesting the results.

members.name: Dr. Elena Moreau
members.expertise: PV yield assessment benchmarking, uncertainty analysis, inter-comparison studies
members.background: Elena is a senior researcher at a European solar R&D center and coordinates the Task 13 exercise that aggregates partner-submitted YAs across climates into a common benchmark workbook and summary plots.
members.private_state: She wants to lock the technical package quickly so she can circulate a near-final benchmark chapter to the wider consortium, and she is trying to avoid reopening methodological debates about partner submissions.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the 'baseline' for a site, they mean the raw partner-submitted yield-assessment spread before any uncertainty-reduction adjustments are applied.
The 'latest site pack' means the version currently stored in the Task 13 SharePoint folder dated with the most recent upload, even if some files inside still carry older filenames.
A handoff of 'site results' naturally includes annual energy values and uncertainty bands by site, not the intermediate monthly loss-factor tables unless someone explicitly asks.
If the economic team says they will 'use the master sheet,' they will copy from her controlled benchmark workbook rather than edit it directly.
A status of 'ready for LCOE' means the benchmark numbers are stable enough for downstream sensitivity use, even if not every explanatory note is finalized.

members.name: Marco Stein
members.expertise: PV project finance modeling, LCOE analysis, uncertainty propagation into cash-flow models
members.background: Marco works at an engineering consultancy that supports investors and EPCs, and within Task 13 he is responsible for translating the benchmarked YA uncertainty scenarios into standardized cash-flow and LCOE case studies.
members.private_state: He needs a clean, comparable input package soon because he has promised a draft economic comparison to his subgroup, and he wants to minimize manual reformatting by his analyst.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the 'baseline,' they mean the central case that has already been normalized into the benchmark framework and is suitable to plug directly into finance models.
The 'latest site pack' means the site package that reflects the last round of comments from site owners, even if it is circulated by email rather than in the shared folder.
A handoff of 'site results' includes the monthly production profile, loss assumptions, and availability conventions needed to derive revenue timing in the cash-flow model.
If everyone agrees to 'work from the master sheet,' that sheet is a shared working artifact that his team can extend with economic tabs without special permission.
A status of 'ready for LCOE' means the inputs are presentation-ready and traceable enough that no later number changes should occur.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to handing over the 'baseline' and comparing uncertainty reduction scenarios against it.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the original benchmark baseline: the raw independent YA results aggregated per site before scenario-based uncertainty tightening.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the cleaned central case already normalized for economic-model ingestion, serving as the default bankable input against which refined scenarios are compared.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In this consortium, 'baseline' is used constantly and usually sounds self-explanatory; both participants are used to adjacent workflows and hear the term as confirming progress rather than as requiring definition.

misalignment_points.topic: Which latest site pack is in scope
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both mention using the 'latest site pack' for the desert and alpine case studies.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the latest upload in the official SharePoint repository, which still contains the April Meteonorm-based weather file and benchmark metadata sheet.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the comment-resolved package sent by the site owner via email last week, which swapped in a revised TMY file and updated curtailment note but has not yet been uploaded centrally.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both believe there is only one obviously current version and the phrase 'latest site pack' feels administratively mundane, so neither expects it to conceal a substantive difference.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on Elena sending 'the site results' so Marco can connect them to the cash-flow model.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes annual yield values, P50/P90-style uncertainty summaries, and site-level benchmark notes, but excludes monthly generation and granular loss-factor breakdowns.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes all of the above plus monthly output profiles, availability treatment, and loss assumptions because those are part of what he considers necessary site results for revenue-shape modeling.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: At a coordination level, 'site results' sounds like a routine deliverable name; each person assumes the omitted details are obviously either part of the package or unnecessary, so the boundary is never tested in the meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the benchmark workbook should be 'ready for LCOE' by the end of next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks 'ready for LCOE' means sufficiently stable for Marco to begin exploratory calculations, while minor explanatory edits and even small number updates can still happen afterward.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks 'ready for LCOE' means frozen enough that his subgroup can produce externally shareable draft comparisons without risk of revising the technical inputs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a simple status checkpoint, and both parties are cooperative and deadline-oriented; because neither wants to appear obstructive, they treat the label as settled rather than unpacking the threshold behind it.

For me, ready for LCOE just means Marco can start using stable numbers next week, even if I still polish notes or make a small correction afterward.
